small_guidance:
- The GEMM dominates at M=1024, N=K=8192. Add larger tiles to the autotune list (e.g. BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=3, and BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64) — current best configs only go to BLOCK_K=64 in one entry; deeper K-tiles help saturate L2 reuse on K=8192.
- Pre-transpose W once (or pass it as B[K,N] contiguous) so the inner load is a contiguous K-stride read; the current `W[n,k]` strided gather over BLOCK_K is the dominant cost. Cache the transposed weight on the module and reuse.
- Drop the `chosen={}` grid trick — instead size partials as `(M, cdiv(N, MIN_BLOCK_N))` and pass NTILES via tensor stride; that removes a Python-side dict mutation per launch and lets autotune pick freely.
large_guidance:
- Make the GEMM kernel persistent and fuse the LSE reduction across N entirely: with M=1024 small, launch one program per M-row tile that streams over all N tiles, keeping a running (max, sumexp) in registers using the online-logsumexp update. This eliminates the partials buffer, the second kernel, and the global-memory round-trip.
- Cache `W^T` (shape [K,N], contiguous in N) as a buffer on the module at init, so the inner GEMM loop loads B contiguously along N for `tl.dot`. Combined with persistence over N, the K=8192 reduction becomes a single sweep per row-tile.
- Fuse the bias add, double-LeakyReLU, and double-GELU into the epilogue of the persistent kernel after the final LSE is computed — store a single fp32 per row directly to `out`, no second kernel launch.
